questions.question: A model API accepts 128K tokens. What does that fact establish by itself?
options: The model uses evidence equally well at every position through 128K.
The request can fit within the advertised input limit, but usable behavior still needs measurement.
The model will outperform retrieval at 128K.
Latency and cost will remain constant through 128K.
questions.explanation: An accepted input length is a transport and serving property. It does not prove retrieval, reasoning, evidence use, latency, or output quality across that window.

questions.question: Why should a long-context test sweep evidence depth as well as context length?
options: To make every prompt contain the same number of tokens.
Because evidence position can change performance even when the total input length is unchanged.
Because middle-position evidence is always easier.
To eliminate the need for repeated trials.
questions.explanation: Position sensitivity can hide behind one aggregate score. A depth sweep exposes beginning, middle, and end behavior at the same length.

questions.question: A candidate passes single-needle retrieval at 64K. Which claim is still unsupported?
options: It can retrieve that kind of unique fact in the tested slices.
It can reliably combine conflicting facts across several documents and cite the controlling evidence.
The prompt fit within the tested input limit.
The evaluator can score the known needle.
questions.explanation: Single retrieval is a useful smoke test, but it does not establish multi-hop reasoning, aggregation, conflict resolution, or citation completeness.

questions.question: A length-by-depth grid has strong average task success, but the 50% depth slice fails the predeclared evidence-use floor. What should the release gate do?
options: Pass because the average is strong.
Delete the middle slice and recompute the average.
Block or constrain the release until the failed critical slice is addressed.
Lower the floor after seeing the result.
questions.explanation: A predeclared slice floor prevents a strong average from hiding a known failure region. The supported operating frontier must exclude or repair that region.

questions.question: When can retrieval-assisted context be preferable to sending every source token directly?
options: When retrieval recall, evidence preservation, and generation quality pass their own product-shaped gates.
Whenever the source collection contains more than one document.
Only when the model has no context window.
Because retrieval removes the need to evaluate grounding.
questions.explanation: Retrieval can stabilize cost and signal density, but it introduces a retrieval-recall boundary. Both retrieval and answer grounding require independent evaluation.

questions.question: What must be versioned to reproduce a long-context evaluation result?
options: Only the model name.
Only the final aggregate score.
The model and tokenizer, prompt, documents and ordering, retrieval state, generation settings, scorer, and case seeds.
Only the advertised context-window size.
questions.explanation: Long-context behavior is sensitive to the full evaluation protocol. Reproducibility requires the candidate, data layout, inference path, and scoring contract.
